# WRF/WPS proof run for the Eyjafjörður wake validation

A working WRF **V4.3.3** + WPS is built and verified in the Docker image
`windfall/wrf:4.3.3` (from `sagunkayastha/wrf` + an `ungrib` recompile —
GRIB2/jasper linking fixed). The Fitch wind-farm scheme (`windfarm_opt`)
is present. This folder holds the Eyjafjörður run deck and drivers.

## Files (generated by `make_rundeck.py` from `designs.py`)
- `namelist.wps` / `namelist.input` — 9/3/1-km nest on the fjord;
  `windfarm_opt=1` on the inner (1-km) domain.
- `wind-turbine-1.tbl` — Fitch turbine spec (hub, rotor, Ct & power
  curves) for the chosen design's turbine (default SAMSETT → Future-20).
- `windturbines.txt` — 24 turbines at real lat/lon (the SAMSETT layout).
- `run_proof.sh` — drives geogrid → ungrib → metgrid → real → wrf, twice
  (turbines off then on).
- `compare_wrf_1d.py` — extracts the Akureyri hub-wind reduction from the
  two `wrfout` files and compares to `model.marginal_reduction`.

## Prerequisites (the two external datasets)
1. **WPS_GEOG static geography** (`/BUILD_WRF/geog.sh` →
   `geog_high_res_mandatory.tar.gz`, **~29 GB**). Mount at
   `/BUILD_WRF/WPS_GEOG`.
2. **Met forcing**: ERA5 (or CARRA) on pressure levels for the case dates
   (default 2022-01-15…16), as GRIB. Mount at `/work/grib`. Set the
   matching `VTABLE` (ERA5 → `Vtable.ECMWF`).

## Run
```bash
docker run --rm --platform linux/amd64 \
  -v "$PWD/wrf":/work \
  -v /path/to/WPS_GEOG:/BUILD_WRF/WPS_GEOG \
  -v /path/to/met_grib:/work/grib \
  windfall/wrf:4.3.3 bash /work/run_proof.sh
python3 wrf/compare_wrf_1d.py wrf/wrfout_d03_baseline.nc wrf/wrfout_d03_turbines.nc
```

## Proof-run results (executed locally, 2026-06-19)
The full real-data chain ran on this Mac for a strong norðanátt
(Jan 1 2022, ERA5 forcing, real DEM), as a tractable 9/3-km, 12-h case
under amd64 emulation: **geogrid → ungrib → metgrid → real → wrf** all
succeed; the no-turbine and with-turbine (full 24-turbine SAMSETT)
integrations both complete. Baseline Akureyri hub wind ≈ 21 m/s.

The earlier zero-thrust/segfault problems were traced to a **malformed
turbine table** (the Fitch reader wants `nval` on line 1, then
`hub diam stc npower`); fixing the format made the drag apply and the
full farm run — no recompile needed.

**Result (compare_wrf_1d.py, figures/wrf_vs_1d.png):** WRF produces a
clear turbine wake — peak ≈ 8-10% pressure reduction at Dalvík/Hrísey
(18-25 km, downstream of the outer cluster) — but it **recovers within
~15-25 km** and is **≈0.2% at Akureyri** (55 km). The 1D model, with its
assumed recovery length L = 55-80 km, instead carries ~23% all the way to
the head. So the mesoscale run does **not** reproduce the 1D
channeled-wake persistence: the "Fjord Effect" recovery length is much
shorter in WRF, and the shielding at Akureyri is essentially negligible
in this case. This is consistent with the low data-derived channeling
fraction (f≈0.31, ridge_stability.py).

**1 km confirmation (proof1km/, figures/wrf_resolution.png):** the same
event re-run with a third nest at **1 km** (`windfarm_opt=1` on d03)
reproduces the 3 km picture almost exactly — peak ~8% at 18-25 km,
≈0.2% at Akureyri. The agreement across resolutions rules out the
obvious objection that 3 km numerical mixing artificially accelerated
the recovery: the short recovery length is **resolution-robust**, not a
coarse-grid artifact. Both WRF runs were executed natively on this Mac
(arm64, MPI/dmpar build, ~8.7× faster than serial).

**Caveats:** one 12-h winter event, single config (SAMSETT). The
multi-event question — does the short recovery hold across the full
norðanátt distribution — is now the decisive remaining test, not
resolution.

## Status / honest scope
The toolchain, deck, drivers, **and the runs themselves are complete on
this machine**: a native arm64 MPI WRF build (`build_arm64/`) ran the
full 9/3/1-km nest for the design event, baseline and 24-turbine, at
both 3 km (`proof/`) and 1 km (`proof1km/`). The Docker `amd64` image
remains the portable/HPC-drop-in path; the native build is what made
the 1-km nest tractable locally. The remaining HPC-scale work is the
multi-event campaign, not a single higher-resolution run.
